Zoran Terzic (director) | products = Rich Energy | website = [https://www.richenergy.com richenergy.com] }} '''Rich Energy''' was a British beverage brand{{Cite web |title=Rich Energy |url=https://richenergy.com |access-date=2024-08-18 |website=Rich Energy |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=Instagram |url=https://www.instagram.com/richenergy/ |access-date=2024-08-18 |website=www.instagram.com}}{{Cite web |title=NEWS: Rich Energy Announced as Haas F1 Team Title Partner {{!}} Haas F1 Team |url=https://www.haasf1team.com/news/news-rich-energy-announced-haas-f1-team-title-partner |access-date=2024-08-18 |website=www.haasf1team.com |language=en}} that was founded in 2015 by [[William John Storey|William Storey]] and an anonymous Austrian scientist. The energy drink project began in 2009 with the development of the product, and the UK distribution company{{Cite web |date=2022-07-22 |title=Controversial ex-F1 sponsor back in hot water |url=https://www.nine.com.au/sport/motorsport/news-2022-former-f1-sponsor-rich-energy-at-centre-of-bizarre-spat-20220721-p5j0f8.html |access-date=2024-07-05 |website=Nine |language=en}} was founded six years later.{{Cite news |last=Gerrard |first=Bradley |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2018/03/30/rich-energy-chief-fell-drinks-business-meeting-mad-scientist/ |title=Rich Energy chief: 'I fell into the drinks business after meeting a mad scientist' |date=2018-03-30 |work=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]] |access-date=2019-06-24}} Information about Rich Energy and its energy drink is very limited. Due to this, the company has been the subject of controversy regarding the existence of its product.{{Cite web |url=https://jalopnik.com/what-you-find-when-you-look-into-rich-energy-the-myste-1833303620 |title=What You Find When You Look Into Rich Energy, the Mystery Sponsor of America's F1 Team |website=Jalopnik |access-date=12 July 2019}} On 16 July 2019, Rich Energy announced that they had renamed their company "'''Lightning Volt Ltd.'''",{{Cite web|title=Lightning Volt Limited - Overview|url=https://beta.companieshouse.gov.uk/company/09791667|access-date=2020-07-07|website=beta.companieshouse.gov.uk}} and on 19 July 2019 a new company was incorporated under the name "Rich Energy Limited".{{Cite web|url=https://beta.companieshouse.gov.uk/company/12112427|title=Rich Energy Limited}} Information filed at [[Companies House]] also revealed that William Storey and Serbian colleague Zoran Terzic had apparently resigned as directors from the newly renamed Lightning Volt Ltd., before being reappointed on 29 August 2019. Storey stated that he had "sold his stake in the legal entity of Rich Energy".{{Cite web|last=Collantine|first=Keith|date=2019-07-16|title=Haas sponsor Rich Energy rebrands as Lightning Volt as CEO quits|url=https://www.racefans.net/2019/07/16/haas-sponsor-rich-energy-rebrands-as-lightning-volt-as-ceo-quits/|access-date=2019-07-17|website=RaceFans}} Matthew Kell was appointed as a new director of the company after Storey's apparent exit.{{Cite web|last=George|first=Patrick|title=Embattled F1 Sponsor Rich Energy Is Now 'Lightning Volt Limited', CEO William Storey Is Out|url=https://jalopnik.com/embattled-f1-sponsor-rich-energy-is-now-lightning-volt-1836415910|access-date=2019-07-18|website=Jalopnik}}{{Cite web |url=https://www.pitpass.com/65220/Rich-Energy-becomes-Lightning-Volt |title=Rich Energy becomes... Lightning Volt |date=2019-07-16 |website=Pitpass.com |access-date=2019-07-18}} In August 2019, Storey bought back shares from Kell to retake a majority shareholding in the company.{{Cite web |url=https://formulaspy.com/f1/william-storey-resumes-control-of-rich-energy-63939 |title=Formula 1 - William Storey resumes control of Rich Energy |date=2019-08-29 |website=FormulaSpy |access-date=2019-10-26}} Lightning Volt Limited was declared insolvent on 27 October 2020, following a petition by a creditor, and a liquidator was appointed on 13 January 2021. == Flavours == * Original (since 2015) * Sugar Free (since 2021) == Sponsorship == === Motorsports === [[File:FIA F1 Austria 2019 Nr. 20 Magnussen 2.jpg|thumb|[[Kevin Magnussen]] driving the Rich Energy-sponsored [[Haas VF-19|VF-19]] at the [[2019 Austrian Grand Prix]]]] In 2017 Rich Energy sponsored British Superbike team True Heroes Racing. In October 2018, Rich Energy became the title sponsor of [[Haas F1 Team]] as Rich Energy Haas F1 Team.{{Cite web |url=https://www.sportsbusinessdaily.com:443/en/Global/Issues/2018/10/26/Marketing%20and%20Sponsorship/Haas%20Rich%20Energy.aspx |title=Haas F1 Signs Rich Energy As Title Sponsor |date=26 October 2018 |website=www.sportsbusinessdaily.com |access-date=2019-06-23}}{{Cite web |url=https://www.thedrive.com/accelerator/24506/haas-f1-signs-soft-drink-startup-rich-energy-as-2019-title-sponsor |title=Haas F1 Signs Soft Drink Startup Rich Energy as 2019 Title Sponsor |last=Gilboy |first=James |website=The Drive |date=27 October 2018 |access-date=2019-06-23}} Originally, the company intended to get a sponsorship deal with [[Williams Grand Prix Engineering|Williams]]. However, it was unclear whether the team rejected the offer{{Cite web |url=https://wtf1.com/post/rich-energy-ceo-hits-out-at-claims-that-his-company-isnt-legitimate/ |title=Rich Energy CEO Hits Out At Claims That His Company Isn't Legitimate |last=Eagles |first=James |date=7 February 2019 |website=WTF1 |access-date=2019-06-24}}{{Cite web |url=http://www.williamsgpnews.com/news/rich-energy-boss-talks-williams-deal/ |title=Rich Energy boss talks Williams deal |last1=M |first1=Jadran |last2=ekic |date=2019-02-09 |website=Williams Grand Prix News |access-date=2019-06-24}} or Rich Energy simply changed their mind.{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/f1/story/_/id/27221746/the-bizarre-haas-rich-energy-saga-explained |title=The bizarre Haas-Rich Energy saga explained |first=Nate |last=Saunders |date=March 3, 2020 |website=ESPN |access-date=March 7, 2020}} Rich Energy also attempted to purchase [[Force India]] for £100 million which had been put into [[Administration in United Kingdom law|administration]] by the [[High Court in London|High Court]] at the time. Storey claimed the deal had been finalised but this was denied by the Indian racing team.{{Cite web |url=https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/rich-energy-launch-official-100m-takeover-force-india-william-storey |title=Rich Energy launch official £100m takeover of Force India |website=www.linkedin.com |access-date=2019-06-24}}{{Cite web |url=https://www.thedrive.com/accelerator/18738/sahara-force-india-denies-possibility-of-being-sold-to-new-investors |title=Sahara Force India Denies Possibility of Being Sold to New Investors |last=Perez |first=Jerry |website=The Drive |date=23 February 2018 |access-date=2019-06-23}}{{Cite web |url=https://www.richmondandtwickenhamtimes.co.uk/news/16089935.rich-energy-finalising-purchase-of-formula-one-team-force-india/ |title=Exclusive Image: Richmond-based company finalising purchase of Formula One team Force India |website=Richmond and Twickenham Times |access-date=2019-06-24}} In 2019 Rich Energy also sponsored British [[Indy NXT|Indy Lights]] driver [[Toby Sowery]] and [[Australian Endurance Championship|Australian GT]] drivers Rio Nugara and David Russell.{{Cite web|title=Rich Energy colours for Australian GT Audi|url=https://speedcafe.com/rich-energy-colours-for-australian-gt-audi/|website=speedcafe.}} In February 2020, Rich Energy was announced as the new title sponsor of [[British Superbike Championship]] race entrant OMG Racing.{{Cite web |url=https://www.autosport.com/tt/news/148256/exhaas-sponsor-rich-energy-joins-bike-team |title=Ex-Haas Formula 1 sponsor Rich Energy to back road racing squad OMG |last=Duncan |first=Lewis |website=Autosport.com |access-date=2020-03-23}} In July 2020, Rich Energy was announced as a sponsor of [[BTCC]] driver [[Michael Crees]], who drives for [[BTC Racing]].{{cite web |url=https://btcracing.co.uk/fan-favourite-british-touring-car-star-michael-crees-links-up-with-rich-energy/ |title=Fan-Favourite British Touring Car Star Michael Crees Links Up With Rich Energy |website=btcracing.co.uk |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811150505/https://btcracing.co.uk/fan-favourite-british-touring-car-star-michael-crees-links-up-with-rich-energy/ |archive-date=2020-08-11}} In 2021, Rich Energy branding could be seen on the [[BTCC]] Vauxhall Astras of [[Jason Plato]] and [[Daniel Lloyd (racing driver)|Daniel Lloyd]]. In April 2022, Storey did a deal for Rich Energy to become title sponsor of BTC Racing in the British Touring Car Championship.{{Cite web |last=TouringCarTimes |date=2022-04-12 |title=BTC Racing announces Rich Energy backing |url=https://www.touringcartimes.com/2022/04/12/btc-racing-announces-rich-energy-backing/ |access-date=2024-10-02 |website=TouringCarTimes |language=en-US}} === Boxing === Rich Energy has sponsored Jay Carrigan-McFarlane{{Cite web|title=Meet the British heavyweight on the Gennady Golovkin-Daniel Jacobs bill|url=https://boxingnewsonline.net/news/meet-the-british-heavyweight-on-the-gennady-golovkin-daniel-jacobs-bill/|website=Boxing News Online}}, Lucas Browne, Jim Walker, Phil Campion and [[Gennady Golovkin]]. === Other === In 2016 British yachtsman [[Alex Thomson (sailor)|Alex Thomson]] signed a sponsorship deal with Rich Energy.{{Cite web|title=Alex Thomson Racing Signs Rich Energy Deal|url=https://sportindustry.co.uk/news-categories/news/alex-thomson-racing-signs-rich-energy-deal/|website=SIG}} In 2021-2022 Rich Energy sponsored Jamaican Bobsleigh and Skeleton Federation. == Controversies == === Company legitimacy === Controversies regarding Rich Energy's credibility began to spread in the days following Rich Energy's attempt to purchase the [[Force India]] [[Formula One]] team. Internet forums and social media posts questioned the legitimacy of the company.{{Cite web |url=https://jalopnik.com/what-you-find-when-you-look-into-rich-energy-the-myste-1833303620 |title=What You Find When You Look Into Rich Energy, the Mystery Sponsor of America's F1 Team |last=King |first=Alanis |website=Jalopnik |access-date=2019-06-24}} Then-CEO William Storey had denied the claims multiple times, stating that Rich Energy had produced 90 million drink cans, and that it was backed by £4 billion worth of endorsements{{Cite web |url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/haas-rich-energy-doubters-moon-landing/4333920/ |title=Haas title sponsor likens doubters to moon landing truthers |website=www.motorsport.com |access-date=2019-06-24}} despite there being no financial information corroborating this claim and the company's financial documentation was available through [[Companies House]].{{Cite web |title=Rich Energy Limited- Filing history |url=https://beta.companieshouse.gov.uk/company/09791667/filing-history |access-date=2019-06-24 |website=beta.companieshouse.gov.uk}} === Copyright infringement === In May 2019, Rich Energy Ltd. was involved in a court case with [[Whyte Bikes]] due to the [[stag]]-[[antler]] logo used by Rich Energy bearing too close a resemblance to the logo used by the bicycle company. Rich Energy lost the case, with the judge declaring that Rich Energy had misled the court by claiming they did not previously know about Whyte Bikes.{{Cite web |url=https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/143396/haas-title-sponsor-loses-legal-case-over-stag-logo |title=Haas F1 team title sponsor Rich Energy loses legal case over stag logo |last=Cooper |first=Adam |website=Autosport.com |access-date=2019-06-24}}{{Cite web |url=https://www.pinkbike.com/news/whyte-bikes-win-legal-battle-against-haas-f1-teams-title-sponsor-rich-energy.html |title=Whyte Bikes Win Legal Battle Against Haas F1 Team's Title Sponsor, Rich Energy |date=2019-05-14 |website=Pinkbike |access-date=2019-06-24}} On 18 July 2019, the Rich Energy [[Twitter]] account leaked alleged court documents, suggesting that the company, as well as William Storey, would be facing legal proceedings by [[Austria]]n energy drink company [[Red Bull GmbH]] in relation to Rich Energy's advertising slogan because Storey was regularly using Red Bull's own advertising slogans against them.{{Cite web |url=https://www.gpfans.com/en/articles/42313/red-bull-suing-ex-rich-energy-chief-according-to-leak/ |title=Red Bull suing ex-Rich Energy chief, according to leak |website=GPfans |access-date=2019-07-18}} === Sponsorship with Haas F1 Team === On 10 July 2019, the Rich Energy Twitter account announced that the company had ended its sponsorship deal with [[Haas F1 Team]] due to the team's poor performance and [[Formula One Group]]'s politics and attitude.{{Cite web |url=https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/144704/rich-energy-says-it-has-terminated-haas-f1-deal |title=Rich Energy says Haas F1 deal terminated, citing "poor performance" |last=Cooper |first=Adam |website=Autosport.com |access-date=2019-07-12}} The announcement from the energy drink brand came as "a surprise" to [[Guenther Steiner]], Haas's team principal at the time.{{Cite news |last=Collantine |first=Keith |url=https://www.racefans.net/2019/07/11/surprised-haas-will-run-rich-energy-logos-at-silverstone/ |title="Surprised" Haas will run Rich Energy logos at Silverstone |date=2019-07-11 |work=RaceFans |access-date=2019-07-11}} The following day, the company's shareholders disowned the announcement, stating that the apparent termination of the sponsorship deal was "the rogue actions of one individual". The company also stated that it was "in the process of removing the individual from all executive responsibilities".{{Cite web |url=https://www.grandprix247.com/2019/07/11/rich-energy-rogue-actions-of-one-individual/ |title=Rich Energy: Rogue actions of one individual | GRAND PRIX 247 |date=11 July 2019 |access-date=2019-07-11}}{{Cite web |url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/rich-energy-remove-storey-embarrassment-haas/4492643/ |title=Rich Energy shareholders blame "rogue individual" for Haas tweet |website=www.motorsport.com |access-date=2019-07-11}} William Storey later accused his company's shareholders of "mounting a coup" in relation to the Haas F1 Team sponsorship.{{Cite web |url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/rich-energy-ceo-haas-coup-tweet/4492868/ |title=Rich Energy CEO accuses shareholders of mounting "coup" |website=www.motorsport.com |access-date=2019-07-11}} On 9 September 2019, a day after the [[2019 Italian Grand Prix|Italian Grand Prix]], Haas announced the termination of the deal with Rich Energy with immediate effect.{{Cite web |url=https://www.haasf1team.com/news/haas-f1-team-statement-rich-energy |title=Haas F1 Team Statement on Rich Energy |date=9 September 2019 |website=Haas F1 Team |access-date=9 September 2019}} == References == {{reflist}} === Bibliography === * {{Cite book |last1=Blackstock |first1=Elizabeth |last2=King |first2=Alanis |title=Racing with Rich Energy: How a Rogue Sponsor Took Formula One for a Ride |date=2022 |publisher=McFarland & Company, Inc., Publishers |isbn=978-1-4766-4792-0 |location=Jefferson, North Carolina |oclc=1346531926}} [[Category:Drink companies of the United Kingdom]] [[Category:British companies established in 2015]] [[Category:Energy drinks]]

Rich Energy was a British beverage brand that was founded in 2015 by William Storey and an anonymous Austrian scientist. The energy drink project began in 2009 with the development of the product, and the UK distribution company was founded six years later. Information about Rich Energy and its energy drink is very limited. Due to this, the company has been the subject of controversy regarding the existence of its product.
On 16 July 2019, Rich Energy announced that they had renamed their company "Lightning Volt Ltd.", and on 19 July 2019 a new company was incorporated under the name "Rich Energy Limited". Information filed at Companies House also revealed that William Storey and Serbian colleague Zoran Terzic had apparently resigned as directors from the newly renamed Lightning Volt Ltd., before being reappointed on 29 August 2019. Storey stated that he had "sold his stake in the legal entity of Rich Energy". Matthew Kell was appointed as a new director of the company after Storey's apparent exit. In August 2019, Storey bought back shares from Kell to retake a majority shareholding in the company.
Lightning Volt Limited was declared insolvent on 27 October 2020, following a petition by a creditor, and a liquidator was appointed on 13 January 2021.
